doc.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019

title: Shearing's musicianship, showmanship and humor
summary: Piltzecker values Shearing's taste and how he handled an audience, with his blindness jokes; Rowe recalls Joe Williams's interview.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: It’s funny, my experience with that band and with George was more impactful actually to me, years after I left the band. It’s where I really started to think about it. Where it happened you know and how much I really learned. I didn’t think about how much I learned by the example of sort of stellar musicianship and good taste. That’s what he — you know, and how to handle an audience, he had his typical jokes but, you know, “Have you been blind all your life?” “Not yet.” “The proceeds from tonight’s concert will be going to the blind. Not all the blind” you know, the typical — he had a shtick you know.

Yes. He told this funny — Joe Williams interviewed him for us. And it was a great session and he told some things about his childhood and playing in an all-blind band. And we weren’t sure that — is he making this stuff up?
I read that interview in this archive.
Even Joe said, “Oh come on, George.”
Yeah he started at the beginning.
